newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gold seen headed for downside tests - Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Gold seen headed for downside tests - Dresdner.

text.p: Gold bullion, which fixed sharply lower at $345 an ounce on Friday morning, was set for further tests of the downside, a weekly precious metals report from Dresdner Kleinwort Benson bank said.
The bank pegged support at $341, then $335.
The London morning fix was the lowest since Sept 14, 1993.
Dresdner said gold might not breach the 1993 low of $326 but needed fund support, which was lacking because bonds and shares markets looked more attractive.
Mark prices of gold were volatile after a week of gold gyrations and dollar swings.
They were last at 564 marks per ounce, down from the 590 marks reached earlier this week, which was the highest mark level since June 1996.
Dresdner recommended measured sales below 560 marks.
Demand for gold leases had risen amid sales from funds, producers and possibly from central banks.
It put one month rates at 1.75 percent but noted a number of transactions had been arranged at two percent.
